paras: The killing of Tom Irvin was the shooting death of a Black man by a sheriff's posse at Alpine, Texas, reported in a dispatch dated January 11, 1903. Irvin had been accused of killing a Mexican man at a dance, and the posse killed him at a house where, by the officers' account, he had barricaded himself and refused to surrender.

According to the Alpine dispatch, the shooting took place at a Black dance held "across the track" in a part of town the report called "Mexico." Irvin was described as "a negro, later from Gollad," probably Goliad, Texas.

The dispatch stated that Irvin called an unnamed Mexican man out of the dance hall and shot him through the heart, killing him. Sheriff Walton came to the scene and, after an investigation, deputized a posse. The posse found Irvin barricaded in the house of Oliver Canada and, in the report's words, "had to kill him before he would surrender." The size of the posse and how the killing was carried out are not given.
No report of an inquest or of any inquiry into the posse's actions appears in the coverage.

The episode is known from a single short item in the Houston Daily Post of January 12, 1903, printed on page six under the headline "NEGRO KILLED BY OFFICERS." Its subheading, "He Called a Mexican From a Dance House and Killed Him," led with the accusation against Irvin, and the item gave only the officers' version, presenting the killing as forced by his refusal to surrender. The dispatch named the Mexican victim only as "unknown," and no other report from the white press or from the Black press was found.

reader.title: Killing of Tom Irvin
bases: A sheriff's deputized posse pursued Tom Irvin after a shooting and killed him at a house where he had barricaded himself (A1).

Irvin was killed by a posse deputized by the sheriff while, by the officers' account, resisting arrest, which the report presents as a lawful arrest attempt rather than mob action (A1). The posse's size is not stated, and the only account is the officers' side.
Only one report, a Houston Daily Post dispatch from Alpine, was found in either press (A1).
